svg.text: Raspberry Pi Wiring: Buck Converter Power, Switch & LED
Pin numbers are physical (BOARD) positions on the 40-pin header; names are BCM GPIO. Highlighted pins are the ones in use.
1. Powering the Pi through Pins 2 / 6 bypasses its USB input protection. Use a regulated 5
V, 3 A supply and never connect USB power at the same time.
2. SW1 pulls GPIO17 up to 3.3 V through R1 when pressed. Enable the internal pull-down on
GPIO17 so the pin reads low when open.
3. R2 limits LED current to about 4 mA (3.3 V, typical red LED). GPIO18 is driven high to
4. All GPIO are 3.3 V logic. Never apply 5 V to a GPIO pin.
